title: Conjectures: formally verified results on open graph-theory problems
description:
Kernel-checked Lean 4 proofs, graph certificates, independent checkers and papers for results on open problems in graph theory.

Release v1.1.0 adds the paper Every cubic bipartite graph on at most 84 vertices has a cycle of length 4, 8 or 16 (category B: computer-assisted, with the case split and the soundness of the witness checks proved in Lean 4): a cubic bipartite counterexample to the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture has at least 86 vertices, and every cubic bipartite graph of girth at least 10 on at most 88 vertices has a 16-cycle. The search code adapts Julius Tranquilli's MIT-licensed program and keeps the MIT License (folder results/cubic-bipartite-power-of-two-cycles/src); everything else is CC0. The release also contains a draft of Cycles of length 4, 8, 16 and 32 in censuses of cubic graphs.

Release v1.0.0 contained the paper Small graphs without cycles of length a power of two with its formal development: fδ≥3(4) ≤ 73, fδ≥3(5) ≤ 345 and fcubic(6) ≤ 10,498. The proofs use Lean 4.36.0 without Mathlib, without native_decide, and only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

AI systems (Gemini 4 Neon, Claude Opus 5.5; tools Antigravity and Claude Code) assisted substantially; they are not authors.
keywords: cycles of length a power of two
